chunks.arabic_text: ٤ - زَكَرِيَّا، أَبُو يَحْيَى، كَوْكَبُ الدَّمِ، كُوفِيٌّ. ضَعِيفٌ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). قَالَ

translations.en: 4 – Zakariyya, Abū Yaḥyā, Kawkab al-Dam. Kufan. Weak. Narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him). He said:

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Zakariyya ibn Abi Yahya, known as Kawkab al-Dam, as a Kufan narrator of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) who is classified as weak (da'if). His designation highlights the rigorous scrutiny applied to individual narrators within the Shia tradition, where even those who transmitted from the Imams could be deemed unreliable due to memory lapses or minor defects, necessitating careful verification of their reports.
en.seo_question: Who is Kawkab al-Dam and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.زَكَرِيَّا: Zakariyya, a proper name of the narrator
key_terms.أَبُو يَحْيَى: Abū Yaḥyā, the kunya (honorific name) of the narrator
key_terms.كَوْكَبُ الدَّمِ: Kawkab al-Dam, a laqab (nickname) meaning 'Star of Blood'
key_terms.كُوفِيٌّ: Kufan, indicating origin from the city of Kufa
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating lower reliability
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Peace be upon him, an honorific used for the Imams
